strategy.summary: GET /products filters products by a case-insensitive substring of the name (`q`), returns one page at a time using `limit` (default DEFAULT_LIMIT=20, capped at MAX_LIMIT=50) and `offset`, includes `total`, the number of matches, and refuses with 400 a limit or offset that isn't a whole number, or a limit below 1. The tests are Vitest integration tests that start the real server in-process on an OS-chosen port, as test/products.test.js already does, and check search, paging, the cap and the refusals against the fixed in-memory catalogue.
inScope: GET /products query handling: q, limit, offset, total, the limit cap and the 400 refusals
outOfScope: GET /products/:id and POST /orders (not part of this ticket)
The search box UI (the repo has no UI)
assumptions: The code's limit cap MAX_LIMIT=50 is correct and the README's 'up to 100' is out of date (asked as Q1). The tests import MAX_LIMIT and DEFAULT_LIMIT from src/app.js.
Expected data comes from the fixed 120-product catalogue in src/catalogue.js (8 names x 15). For example, 'tea' matches the 15 Teapots and the 15 Tea strainers, 30 in all, in id order.
No service is faked: the real HTTP server from createApp() runs in-process on port 0.
An empty value (`limit=`) counts as not a whole number, and the code refuses it with 400.
openQuestions: The README says limit goes up to 100, but the code caps it at 50. Which is right? (Q1)

risks.description: Paging overlaps or skips results, or total counts the page rather than all matches
risks.mitigation: TC4 checks the exact ids of a page in the middle of the results and that total stays at 30. TC7 checks an offset past the end.

risks.description: An unbounded limit lets a client pull the whole catalogue
risks.mitigation: TC6 asserts that the page size equals the imported MAX_LIMIT.

risks.description: Malformed paging values are accepted silently
risks.mitigation: TC8 to TC10 cover non-numeric, fractional, negative and zero values.

acceptanceCriteria.text: q returns exactly the products whose name contains q, ignoring case; without q every product is listed.
Results are paged with limit and offset, the response's total is the number of all matches, and a limit above the maximum is capped.
A limit or offset that isn't a whole number, or a limit below 1, gets a 400 response.

testCases.title: matches product names containing q in any case
testCases.expected: 200. total is 30, and items are exactly the Teapot 1-15 and Tea strainer 1-15 products, in id order (each name matches ^(Teapot|Tea strainer) \d+$, 30 items).
testCases.rationale: This is the core search behaviour. The mixed-case query proves case-insensitivity.

testCases.title: lists every product when q is absent
testCases.expected: 200. total equals PRODUCTS.length (120), and items are ids 1..DEFAULT_LIMIT in order.
testCases.rationale: With no query, the whole catalogue is listed. This also covers the default page size.

testCases.title: returns no items and a total of 0 when nothing matches q
testCases.rationale: The search can also find nothing. This case covers that.

testCases.title: returns the requested page of matches with the total of all matches
testCases.expected: 200. total is 30, and items are the 6th to 10th tea matches by id (ids 15, 19, 23, 27, 31: Tea strainer 2, Teapot 3, Tea strainer 3, Teapot 4, Tea strainer 4).
testCases.rationale: Proves offset and limit work together on the filtered results, and that total counts all matches, not just the page.

testCases.title: caps a large limit at the maximum page size
testCases.expected: 200. items has MAX_LIMIT entries (ids 1..MAX_LIMIT), and total is 120.
testCases.rationale: This case covers the ticket's 'large limits are capped' rule.

testCases.title: returns a full page when limit equals the maximum
testCases.expected: Both responses are 200 with MAX_LIMIT items.
testCases.rationale: Checks both sides of the cap boundary.

testCases.title: returns no items but the full total when offset is past the last match
testCases.rationale: Checks the paging boundary at the end of the results.

testCases.title: refuses a limit that is not a whole number with 400
steps: GET /products?limit=<v> for each of abc, 2.5, -1, 1e2, empty string

testCases.title: refuses a limit of 0 with 400 and accepts a limit of 1
testCases.expected: limit=0 gets 400. limit=1 gets 200 with exactly one item (id 1).
testCases.rationale: Checks both sides of the lower bound on limit.

testCases.title: refuses an offset that is not a whole number with 400
steps: GET /products?offset=<v> for each of abc, 1.5, -1, empty string
testCases.expected: 400 for each invalid value. offset=0 gets 200.
testCases.rationale: Covers validation of offset, with the valid boundary as a control.

strategy.environmentNotes: No external services. The tests start createApp() in-process with listen(0), like the existing test/products.test.js, and run under the existing `npm test` (vitest run).

review.standard: Reuse the repo's helpers... A helper two specs or page objects need goes once in their shared base or a helper module.
review.summary: The in-process server setup (beforeAll createApp/listen(0)/base URL, afterAll close) is copied line for line from test/products.test.js lines 4-13 instead of being moved into a shared test helper both specs import.
review.failureScenario: If server start-up changes (e.g. createApp takes options, or the host must become 127.0.0.1 on an IPv6-less CI), it has to be fixed in two specs; updating only test/products.test.js leaves this file starting the server the old way. Extracting e.g. test/helpers/server.js with a startServer()/stop pair and importing it from both specs removes the copy.

review.standard: Vitest: Parametrisation — use it.each when the behaviour is identical and only the data varies
review.summary: TC8 and TC10 loop over the invalid values inside one test (lines 91-95 and 107-111), so the first failing value stops the test and the rest go unreported.
review.failureScenario: If the app started accepting both 'abc' and '' as limit, the run reports only limit=abc failing; the empty-string regression is hidden until the first is fixed. it.each over the values (with $v in the title) would report each one separately, as would splitting TC6's MAX_LIMIT/MAX_LIMIT+1 loop at line 77.

questions.question: For GET /products, the README says `limit` is capped at 100, but the code caps it at 50 (MAX_LIMIT in src/app.js). Which cap is correct?
questions.assumption: The code's cap (50) is right and the README is out of date. The tests import MAX_LIMIT from src/app.js and assert against it, and I'll list a README fix as a follow-up.
questions.answer: The cap is 50, as the code does. The README is out of date; leave it as it is and test against 50.
